question: What post-subagent completion contract should OpenClaw support, if any, and how should it bound child output/history exposure, announcement mutation or suppression, and delivery-result visibility?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but payload shape, plugin authority, redaction, ordering, timeouts, and interaction with the rejected guard-hook pull request are public API and security-boundary choices that automation should not lock in.

options.title: Typed Plugin Delivery Hook
options.body: Add a bounded typed hook at the post-child-result/pre-announcement seam with explicit metadata, redaction, timeout, audit, and return semantics for enrichment or suppression.

options.title: Generic Delivery Boundary First
options.body: Fold this into a broader product-driven output or delivery boundary so subagent completion filtering does not become a one-off public API.

options.title: Observation-Only Event
options.body: Expose only a non-mutating completion event and leave announcement mutation or suppression to separate delivery-policy work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13911.

recommendation.title: Typed Plugin Delivery Hook
recommendation.body: Add a bounded typed hook at the post-child-result/pre-announcement seam with explicit metadata, redaction, timeout, audit, and return semantics for enrichment or suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current decision signal is the core thread-binding work plus the review comment closing the overlapping guard-hook pull request in favor of a product-driven delivery boundary.
